what_was_done: run_checkpoint now wraps the product stops, every _close_story and the flush in try/except, appending each fault to errors, and calls the release path (_release_path: run_set(agents), lock_release, run_end) in a finally; next is computed after the release. A corrupt closure and a StoreBusy closure_update now answer ok:false, exit 1, with an empty lock and an ended run, instead of escaping as exit 2 'internal error' with the lock held.

survey story refuses with exit 2 when project.layout is hub, when the one open cycle's kind is hotfix (its stories are cut from hotfix/<version>, not the integration head), and when --subject is empty (a usage refusal, not 'story  is not in the open wave' at exit 1). The --cycle refusal no longer indexes an empty cycle list: '--cycle X' with no cycle open is a usage refusal too.
where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/survey.py; test next/tests/unit/test_survey.py::test_survey_unbuilt_is_exit_2_with_whole_object (hub, hotfix, missing --subject, --cycle with none open)

what_was_done: Every 'worktree add' in the library (create_story, set_integration, detached) now runs 'git worktree prune' first, so a worktree directory removed outside git no longer leaves a registration that wedges every later add. Re-admission after a by-hand rmtree and set_integration after a by-hand rmtree both succeed.

Classified as not_permitted only when git's stderr contains 'Operation not permitted'; the word 'sandbox' in the command's path arguments no longer misclassifies an ordinary failure, which answers code 'git'. The not_permitted message still carries the word 'sandbox' and git's own line (ORDER.md rule 11).

Re-recorded P3REQ-07, P3OPS-07, P3OPS-08, P3REQ-02, P3OPS-10 and D33-21 as left-for-builder, each naming the story-path part that is done and the remainder with its owning package (other surveys G5/S2a; non-story stages S3 widened; readiness ordering G5/W6; the route row and new spec decision S3 widened and S4; delivery.detail and packets G4a). findings.py build rerun; the by-package lists carry them again.
where: rewrite/findings/outcomes/step3-survey-fix.json (six entries below); regenerated rewrite/findings/ledger.json and rewrite/findings/by-package/

what_was_done: New test: the story admitted in run A is refused by require_story(root, B, story) with reason story_not_in_run while a second live run B holds nothing and the closure, base and worktree exist. Dropping the story= argument from run_require fails this test (the refusal disappears).
Both cited tests now assert that json.dumps(closure) holds no str(root): the admission closure test and the checkpoint's closes-delivered-story test.

The correcting command is now 'git branch --set-upstream-to=<remote>/<branch> <branch>' (no branch named twice, which git refuses with 'too many arguments to set new upstream'), and the test parses the command out of the message and runs it. create_story's not_descendant advice now names a remedy that works: delete the branch (git branch -D <branch>) and admit the story again, which cuts it from the target head and records that base; verify_story's rewritten-history message points at restoring the commits or recording the rewritten base as delivery does after a rebase.
where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/worktrees.py (_remote_head, create_story, verify_story); test next/tests/unit/test_worktrees.py::test_target_head_local_and_pr (runs the printed command), ::test_verify_story_refusals (asserts the branch -D remedy)

what_was_done: The survey admits an open-wave story with admitted_by='plan'; a run id in admitted_by means an out-of-plan admission through gate plan --story or story new-fix. admit itself only writes admitted_by on a fresh closure, so a re-survey does not overwrite an earlier admission's value. Test asserts the closure's admitted_by is 'plan' after a survey.

Route row 15 now lists the decision ids in args.decisions (D10), not only in the reason text, and 'could run' is preconditions.check(root, 'story', subject, cycle, hooks_alive=None) — a story whose depends_on are undelivered no longer counts as runnable, so an open decision on another story still fires the decisions row. Tests assert args.decisions and the dependency case.

story_path and integration_path derive from classify_worktree (ORDER rule 7), and story_path refuses ids outside the story grammar; story_unit.position, story_unit.build and checkpoint._head_of call story_path instead of rebuilding root/.worktrees/<story>; the criticality enum in admission comes from the policy's [story.frontmatter] row.

With no open cycle, the cycle-scoped precondition rows answer 'no cycle is open' without the cycle-scoped reads (a story with depends_on no longer crashes with exit 2 'internal error: StoreRefused'); '--cycle X' with no cycle open is worded without indexing; checkpoint maps StoreRefused from run_read to the unknown-run refusal ('no run ...'), so checkpoint --run ../x is exit 2 with the whole object.

story_unit._gate no longer swallows every exception: only the absence of evidence is None, a corrupt record or a faulty registered gate rises out of position(), and the survey reports the fault at exit 1 with ok:false ('the story could not be admitted' / 'the survey could not build the story unit', naming the corrupt record) instead of silently lowering the position and rerunning stages.
A run with no stories reports status 'partial', on the live path and on the ended-run read path (D8); all([]) no longer reads as done. Tested on both paths.

Added the test the plan's section 7 names, test_position_reviewed_from_closure_verdict (a demo story whose converged verdict covers the head is reviewed; a verdict that does not cover the head leaves the story at green), and test_kind_without_red_gate_starts_at_red for D6's other half.

remove_story(delete_branch=True) deletes by the configured branch name ([branches].story through branch_name), pruning the stale registration first, so a call killed between the worktree removal and 'branch -D' deletes the branch on the retry; the test rmtrees the worktree by hand and then deletes the branch.

Settled the target-branch meaning: the schema's delivery.branch description now says the branch the story is delivered to — the target branch, require_story's 'target' — which admission records and delivery re-records after a rebase (the code and topics/worktrees.md already said this).
records/run.md now says the survey records each story unit it returns in the run record's stories (with P3BLD-23 named), and commands/survey.md's Writes says it beside the run record.

The checkpoint writes the delivered closure's closed field as the ISO stamp of the checkpoint (not a boolean), and records/closure.md says so: a story's closed is the stamp of the checkpoint that closed it, while the cycle record's closed is the close date. The test asserts a Z-stamped string.
